clue.text: Posh money I had changed

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Posh money I had changed (3-2-3)': money = L plus an anagram of I HAD gives only five letters; the wordplay needs a second 'had' (AHDIDAH), a word apparently dropped in OCR, more than a three-letter correction

clue.text: Following no rules, managed a climb with style

indicators.note: in a down clue, to climb is to go upwards, so the words managed a are read from the bottom up

parts.note: managed, as in ran a business, gives RAN
chic means style or elegance

explanation.surface: A rebel climber who ignores the rules but scales the rock with panache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climb' reads managed a from the bottom up, which works because this is a down light; a rock climber with style is the false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic behaviour is lawless, keeping to no rules or order at all.

clue.text: Waste some time after losing a military offender

parts.note: a waste is a desert, a barren tract

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone wasting time after losing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes the a out of the word for some time; 'Waste' looks like a verb but is the noun for barren land.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter is a soldier who abandons his post, an offence under military law.

clue.text: Daughter has to admit being unhappy

parts.note: to own (up) is to admit or confess

explanation.surface: A daughter feels unhappy at having to confess something.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down is a common idiom for being low in spirits or sad.

clue.text: Crazy message to support country dance

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: the hay (or hey) is an old English country dance
a wire is a telegram, a message

explanation.surface: A message sent in support of folk dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts WIRE below HAY in the down light. The HAY is an old English rustic dance with weaving figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone haywire is an idiom for out of control or crazy.

clue.text: Field Marshal to veto eating European vegetable

parts.note: Sir John French was a British Field Marshal in the First World War

indicators.note: eating says one piece swallows another, so the word for veto takes in a letter

parts.note: to veto is to ban

explanation.surface: A senior officer refuses to let a continental eat his vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts E inside BAN to make BEAN. Field Marshal Sir John French commanded the British army in France in 1914.
explanation.definitionFit: The French bean is a common green vegetable, the pod of the kidney bean plant.

clue.text: Groom — man working towards union of characters

indicators.note: working means being put to work and reshaped, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A bridegroom moving towards marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A monogram is a design made by joining or interlacing initials, letters combined into one figure.

clue.text: Sleeping pill concocted in tiny chop

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture made up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A sleeping tablet hidden in a small cut of meat, perhaps to drug a guard dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' rearranges TINY CHOP; the page's 'concealed' differs by three letters and gives no wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnotic is the pharmacological noun for a drug that induces sleep.

clue.text: I am prepared to interrupt an expression of grief and bitterness

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a cry is a sound of grief or pain
I'm on, as in ready to go along with something, means I am prepared

explanation.surface: Someone ready to break into another's mourning, with bitter feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to interrupt' puts the phrase for I am prepared (I'm on, as in 'you're on') inside the expression of grief; 'prepared' looks like an anagram signal but is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is bitterness or ill feeling in speech or manner.

clue.text: About to employ method to make road up

parts.note: CA is short for circa, about
to employ is to use
a way is a method

explanation.surface: Advice on how to repair a road under works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'road up' looks like British roadworks; here it is a road raised up.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a raised road or track across low or wet ground.

clue.text: Stop kidding, presumably, and relax

definitions.meaning: to wind someone up is to kid them, so stopping it is jokingly the opposite phrase
to unwind or ease off after effort

explanation.surface: Tells a joker to cut it out and calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: Winding down is an idiom for relaxing gradually after activity.

clue.text: Discussions to value Devonshire estate

parts.note: chats are informal discussions
worth is value

explanation.surface: Talks to value a ducal property.
explanation.walkthrough: CHATSWORTH, in Derbyshire, is the country house and estate of the Dukes of Devonshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatsworth House is the seat of the Duke of Devonshire, so it is his estate.

clue.text: They generally divide working days in small pieces

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
knights are chessmen, pieces on the board

explanation.surface: Breaking the work week into little bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' suggests fragments; it is chess pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeknights are the evenings falling between consecutive working days, separating them.

clue.text: Fog can make you worry

definitions.meaning: a sea mist, especially on the North Sea coast

explanation.surface: Bad weather makes one anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fret is a coastal fog, and to fret is to worry.

clue.text: Red mark on the skin's permitted

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
let means permitted

explanation.surface: A red blemish on the skin is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright shade of red.

clue.text: Water controlled by this son who rules the roost?

parts.note: the top cock is the dominant bird that rules the roost

explanation.surface: A domineering son lords it over the household.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopcock is a valve that controls the flow of water in a pipe.

clue.text: Publicises excursion and its possible starting place

parts.note: airs means broadcasts or makes public
a trip is an excursion

explanation.surface: Advertising a trip and where it might begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to the excursion: a flight might set off from a landing strip.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a runway from which a flight may take off.

clue.text: About one horse in 200 is made of clay

indicators.note: in puts the turned pieces inside the numeral

parts.note: CC is 200 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the pieces after it are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: Roughly one horse in two hundred is made of clay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns one horse round, and 'in' sets it between the two halves of the Roman 200; 'About' here is reversal, not C or RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramic describes pottery and objects of fired clay.

clue.text: Pictures restaurant put up on top of table: that's not natural

parts.note: pictures are art

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means written upwards

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: Paintings placed on a restaurant table, an artificial arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns CAFE upwards to EFAC; 'top of' gives T from table.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is a man-made object, something not occurring naturally.

clue.text: American intrigues behind closed doors

indicators.note: intrigues means schemes or plots, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An American plots in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal phrase meaning held in private, not in open court.

clue.text: Catches up with an old Greek

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written upwards

parts.note: traps means catches

explanation.surface: Someone catches up with an ancient Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the word for catches upwards, since this is a down light; 'Catches up with' looks like a phrase but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan was a citizen of Sparta, a city state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Magog regarded to some extent as a giant

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Magog, of Gog and Magog, viewed as a giant.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are legendary giants, so the surface's 'giant' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore.

clue.text: In a word, a breast requiring cosmetic surgery?

definitions.meaning: written as one word, abreast means level, neck and neck
minor plastic surgery to tighten the body

explanation.surface: A breast that needs plastic surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Nip and tuck is an idiom for level in a race, and a slang term for cosmetic surgery.

clue.text: He has a small house and business — endlessly races back to it

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: back says the trimmed word is read in reverse
endlessly says the last letter is lost

parts.note: a regatta is a series of boat races

explanation.surface: A man with a little house and a firm keeps racing back to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the word for races and 'back' then turns it round; regattas are rowing or sailing races.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottager is a person who lives in a cottage, a small country house.

clue.text: Tall pine

explanation.definitionFit: Long means tall in stature, and to long is to pine for something.

clue.text: Janus was deceitful

definitions.meaning: the Roman god Janus is pictured with faces looking both ways

explanation.surface: The Roman god was dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Janus literally had two faces, and two-faced is an idiom for hypocritical.

clue.text: Talk about home with each drink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: chat is talk
in means at home

explanation.surface: Chatting about home over a drink with everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the word for talk around home; in for at home is a standard crossword equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: China tea is tea made from leaves grown in China, a drink.

clue.text: Head' covering needs patching badly

indicators.note: badly means done wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hat that needs mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges PATCHING. The apostrophe after 'Head' is a scanning stray.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a cap worn on the head in bed.
